December - January Bond and Certificate Maturities

On November 30, 1949, the Secretary of the Treasury announced that a new issue of 1-3/8 percent Treasury notes to mature in four and one-quarter years would be offered on December 5. The notes were to be offered in exchange for the three series of Treasury bonds, which, on August 12, had been called for redemption on December 15, and also for the one-year 1-1/4 percent certificates of indebtedness, Series H-1949, maturing December 15, 1949. The three series of maturing bonds totaled $4,375 million and the maturing certificates amounted to $519 million, which together totaled $4,894 million.

The Secretary also announced on November 30 that holders of the one-year 1-1/4 percent certificates of indebtedness, Series A-1950, which will mature January 1, would be offered a one-year 1-1/8 percent certificate in exchange.

Subscription books for the new Treasury notes, Series A-1954, were opened on December 5 and were closed at the close of business on December 8. The notes were dated December 15, 1949, and bear interest from that date at the rate of 1-3/8 percent, payable on a semiannual basis on September 15, 1950, and thereafter on March 15 and September 15 in each year
Note: Details of Treasury market financing operations are shown in the tables on "Offerings" and "Disposition", respectively, of marketable issues of bonds, notes,

until the principal amount becomes payable on March 15, 1954. The notes were issued in bearer form only, with interest coupons attached, in denominations of $1,000, $5,000, $10,000, $100,000, and $1,000,000.
Call of 2 Percent Treasury Bonds of 1950-52

On November 14, the Secretary announced that all outstanding 2 percent Treasury bonds of 1950-52, dated October 19, 1942, are called for redemption on March 15, 1950. The announcement stated that holders of these bonds may, in advance of the redemption date, be offered the privilege of exchanging all or part of their called bonds for other interest-bearing obligations of the United States, in which event public notice will hereafter be given.

Treasury bills maturing in November were refunded in the full amount of $4.0 billion. Each issue amounted to $1,000 million. The issue of November 25 was the eleventh consecutive rollover. The successive average rates of discount on the four November offerings, beginning with that dated November 3, were 1.063 percent, 1.074 percent, 1.056 percent, and 1.052 percent.

Monthly data relating to capital movements between the United States and foreign countries as reported by banks, bankers, and brokers throughout the United States appear in the first four sections of "Capital Movements". Supplementary data are presented at less frequent intervale in Section V. All reports are made initially to the Federal Reserve Banks, which forward consolidated figures to the Treasury.

Section I contains the historical summary of principal types of monthly data on capital movements, beginning with 1935 when the information was first compiled. Each type is then broken down into its chief components in the same chronological detail. Section II supplies a summary by countries, showing a geographic breakdown for recent months of the same principal series and most of the same components. Foreign debit and credit balances in brokerage accounts also are shown by countries.

Section III presents data by countries for certain components of total short-term claims and liabilities and total long-term security transactions. This information is given for the latest month for which final figures are available. Similar information for the latest month for which preliminary figures are available is presented in Section III A. "Short-term" as used in all tables on capital movements refers to original maturities of one-year or less, and "long-term" refers to all other maturities. Section IV contains data for recent months on outstanding contracts of banks for forward purchases and sales of foreign exchange.

Section V presents in Table 1 information by countries on short-term claims on and liabilities to foreigners as reported quarterly by exporters, importers, and industrial and commercial concerns in the United States. This information was published for the first time in the October 1949 issue of the "Treasury Bulletin", covering quarterly periods from September 30, 1946, through December 31, 1946. An explanation of the figures appeared in the headnote on page 49 of that issue. Later data will be published in subsequent issues. Table 2 in Section V supplies information by countries on long-term claims on and liabilities to foreigners as reported by banks and bankers in the United States. These data are collected along with those on short-term balances. However, since the amounts involved represent only a small part of the total long-term investment position of the United States, and the figures exclude by definition the banks' holdings of long-term securities suitable for trading in public securities markets, they have not been published heretofore, nor are they incorporated in the regular monthly series on capital movements. Table 2 appears for the first time in the current issue of the "Treasury Bulletin" and gives data for the end of the calendar years 1942 through 1948. Corresponding data will be published for later years.

Publication of detailed figures in the monthly series on capital movements was discontinued between the March 1942 and the November 1945 issues of the "Treasury Bulletin", but data omitted during that period were supplied in the November 1945 issue and supplement.
